newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo aluminium ends mostly higher helped by LME.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo aluminium ends mostly higher helped by LME.

text.p: Tokyo yen-based aluminium futures closed mostly firmer on Thursday as the metal's resilience on the LME, in contrast with copper's overnight decline, sparked some short-covering, traders said.

"People are now less worried about the downside of aluminium (on the LME)," said one trader. "We've seen some short-covering, especially as some contracts saw their life-of-contract lows on Wednesday."
Benchmark June gained 1.5 yen to end at 185.8, while April added 0.5 to 186.1 yen. Others ranged between 1.03 yen higher to 1.5 yen lower. Estimated volume was 2,106 lots.
In London overnight, aluminium clawed up $3 to $1,568 a tonne helped by a reduction in inventories, while flagship copper gave up $132 to finish at 2,236, near a 4-1/2 month low.
